feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -11 & 4 & 6 \\ 7 & 7 & -3 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{3}$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{23}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 7 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -11 & 4 & -2 \\ 7 & 7 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -11 & 4 & 6 \\ 7 & 7 & -3 & -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}.$
